knowledge_point.title: Finding the Magnitude of a Vector-Valued Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
Evaluating the function at $t=\frac{\pi }{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right) & =\left\langle 2\operatorname{cos}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right),\,4\operatorname{sin}\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right),\,6\right\rangle  \\  & =\left\langle 2\cdot \frac{1}{2},\,4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\,6\right\rangle  \\  & =⟨1,\,2\sqrt{3},\,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|r\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right)| & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(2\sqrt{3})}^{2}+(6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+12+36} \\  & =\sqrt{49} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t)⟩$ be the position vector of the eagle. Find the distance between the eagle and its nest at time $t=5\,\text{s},$ rounded to two decimal places.

The eagle is approximately$\,$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m}$ away from its nest after $t=5$ seconds.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since the nest is at the origin, the distance between the bird and its nest at time $t=5$ is $|r(5)|.$

We know that $y(5)=\frac{95}{3}.$ Evaluating the function at $t=5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(5) & =\left\langle \operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{5}{5}\right),\frac{95}{3}\right\rangle  \\  & =\left\langle \frac{\pi }{4},\frac{95}{3}\right\rangle .\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|r(5)| & =\sqrt{{\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right)}^{2}+{\left(\frac{95}{3}\right)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}+\frac{9\,025}{9}} \\  & ≈31.68\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

question.:question/problem: What is the value of $f(t)=\left\langle \frac{4}{t-1},\,1+{t}^{3},\,(t-1)^{4}\right\rangle $ at $t=3?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=3$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) & =\left\langle \frac{4}{3-1},1+{3}^{3},(3-1)^{4}\right\rangle  \\  & =\left\langle \frac{4}{2},1+27,{2}^{4}\right\rangle  \\  & =⟨2,28,16⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the value of $f(t)$ at $t=3$ is the vector $⟨2,28,16⟩.$
